 ORDER

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.376/2022 dated 18.07.2022 registered at Police Station Civil Lines, District Chhatarpur (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 498-A & 306 of IPC.

entities.text: Police Station Civil Lines, District Chhatarpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case and prima facie no case under Section 306 of IPC is made out as the applicant.
The applicant is in custody since 12.12.2022, charge-sheet has been filed and trial will take considerable time to conclude.

He further submits that the applicant is a permanent resident of the district and there is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence;
that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
On these grounds, the applicant may be released on Gayadeen Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023

1 bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

The present applicant, who is the husband of deceased has filed this bail application on the ground that omnibus allegations have been made against him and no case under Section 306 of IPC is made out on that basis.
For this he has relied upon the order dated 16.12.2022 passed by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Cr.R. No.2467/2021 (Rajendra Singh Lodhi & others vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh & another.

entities.text: Cr.R. No.2467/2021 (Rajendra Singh Lodhi & others vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh & another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case the statement of parents, relatives and also the 10 years old daughter of deceased was recorded.
These statements reflect that applicant was in the habit of often beating his wife and in the preceding night of incident he physically assaulted her by kicks and danda.
The deceased committed suicide by laying on the railway track.

Looking to the statement regarding persistent physical assault on the deceased and treating her with cruelty, which resulted in driving her to commit suicide, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Hence, the prayer for grant of bail is rejected.
The M.Cr.C. stands dismissed.
